description:
Found by the fz-kdt.129 build (2026-09-01): fz-kdt.107's subject one
rung up. Between arms that ask ONE question, order was pure fiat (107's
class, cured per-shape by 118/125/127). Between arms whose tests are
NESTED, order costs precision only (129's class, now canonically
seated). Between distinguishable arms whose tests OVERLAP WITHOUT
containment -- e.g. callable sets {A,B} vs {B,C}: a B-carrying value
passes both tests, and seating decides WHICH BODY RUNS. fz-kdt.129
made that fiat DETERMINISTIC (equal rank, cmp_tys tie-break) -- it did
not make it sound. Recorded in specificity_order's doc and
dispatch-matrix.md's Seating section.

THE CURE IS UPSTREAM, same as always: tests that do not overlap unless
domains do -- exact tuple tags (fz-kdt.119) and list-element
discrimination (fz-kdt.107 step 3) shrink the overlap population;
whatever remains after those land gets re-censused here. TO VERIFY
when picked up: construct the {A,B}/{B,C} callable-overlap shape,
check whether current analysis can even mint it (the fz-kdt.125
refuter could not force overlapping callable sets from source), and
measure the corpus overlap population with the question_groups helper.
Sequence after fz-kdt.119.
title: Order between distinguishable arms with OVERLAPPING tests is meaning, not precision
